From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Marissa / Neha — answering inline and adding recommended customer-friendly text.

1) Hosted routing / region pinning — operational behavior: by default, hosted requests are routed to the nearest available region consistent with account configuration. Customers can select a primary processing region in account settings (US, EU, APAC). When a region is pinned to "US", inference and ephemeral artifacts (prompt/response, KV cache) are executed and stored only on US infrastructure (examples: AWS us-east-1, GCP us-central1). Fallback behavior: if capacity in the pinned region is unavailable we will consult the account's policy — default is to queue or rate-limit; for enterprise accounts we can enable a configured fallback to a dedicated compatible region but that requires contractual approval.

Suggested language to share: "Redwood supports region-restricted processing. For hosted accounts you may elect to pin processing to a specific region (e.g., US). When a region is pinned, request processing and ephemeral artifacts are restricted to that region's infrastructure. Cross-region fallback only occurs under explicitly agreed policies and is not performed by default for accounts with region restrictions."

2) Subprocessors — short breakdown:
- Cloud compute: AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2), GCP (europe-west1) — handle model inference and ephemeral caches.
- Storage / backups: S3 (replication configurable per deployment) — backups are region-scoped for pinned accounts; cross-region replication is not enabled by default for pinned-hosted accounts.
- Monitoring / telemetry: Datadog (US/EU deployments), Sentry (error traces) — telemetry uses partial pseudonymization and does not store raw prompt content unless debug mode is enabled by the customer.
- Identity / auth: Okta (US) for enterprise auth.

Suggested language to share: "A current subprocessor inventory (attached) lists vendors and processing locations. We segregate subprocessors by function (compute, storage, telemetry) and document which subprocessors may handle customer request content vs derived telemetry. We will not enable debug-mode capture of raw prompt content without explicit customer opt-in."

3) Replication / DR — default behavior: for hosted, we keep automated backups in the region for pinned accounts. DR copies to other regions are performed only under explicit DR/backup policies and require customer notification or contractual agreement.

Suggested language to share: "Backups are region-oriented and not replicated cross-border by default for accounts that choose regional pinning. Cross-region replication is available as part of a DR package and will be reflected in contract terms."

4) Retention & deletion — controls and SLA:
- Customers can configure retention for request logs and prompt/response artifacts at the account level (example options: 7, 30, 90, 365 days).
- For hosted accounts we offer an enforceable deletion SLA of 30 days with a contractual clause for enterprise agreements (we can put a 30-day deletion clause into the SOW).
- Immediate deletion API: we provide an admin API to request deletion of stored artifacts; once a deletion request is acknowledged, artifacts are removed from primary stores within 72 hours and from backups within 30 days depending on backup cycles (we include this in the SLA).

Suggested language to share: "Redwood supports configurable retention windows and an admin deletion API. For enterprise customers we can contractually guarantee a 30-day deletion SLA for request artifacts; primary stores are purged within 72 hours of an approved deletion request, full backup purging occurs within 30 days per backup cycle."

Let me know if you want me to tone down legalese — I can provide a one-page customer-facing summary plus the CSV inventory.

— Karthik
Head of Product Security (on inference compliance topics)

Hi Danielle — thanks for the questions. Per our internal review (copied Karthik and Neha), here is a concise summary you can share with your Security/Procurement teams: 

1) Region pinning: Redwood supports region selection for hosted accounts. If you pin processing to the US, inference and ephemeral artifacts (prompt/response, KV caches) are processed and stored on US-only infrastructure. Cross-region fallback is not performed by default for pinned accounts and requires contractual approval.

2) Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor inventory (CSV). High-level: cloud compute and inference are hosted on cloud providers in the pinned region (AWS us-east-1 / GCP us-central1 for US), storage/backups are regionally scoped unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled, and telemetry vendors (Datadog / Sentry) are configured per-region with pseudonymization for traces.

3) Replication / DR: Backups for pinned accounts remain in-region by default. Cross-region DR/replication is available as an add-on and will be documented in the SOW.

4) Retention & deletion: Customers can set retention windows (7 / 30 / 90 / 365 days). For enterprise agreements we can include a contractual 30-day deletion SLA: primary stores purged within 72 hours after an approved deletion request; backups removed within a 30-day cycle. We can add explicit wording to your MSA/SOW.
